sections.title: The riot
sections.line: A silversmith's trade, two hours of chanting, a clerk's warning.

themes.note: A power others try to borrow, and cannot.
The Spirit given, and unclean spirits that know the difference.
Luke's refrain, marking each stage the mission clears.
A goddess, a trade, and a city defending both.

references.why: The Samaritans believed without receiving the Spirit too, so Luke is repeating a pattern rather than reporting an Ephesian oddity.
Demons know and shudder; the evil spirit has better information than the exorcists, and knowing the name is not faith.
The third of Luke's growth refrains, marking the mission clearing another stage rather than just reporting success.
Rome is announced here and reached in chapter 28, so this verse sets the course for the rest of Acts.
Paul's line about man-made gods is Israel's standard idol polemic, which Demetrius hears as a threat to trade.

purpose.statement: Luke wants us to know the Spirit is given rather than conjured, because the name works for those baptised into it and mauls those who borrow it.
He wants us to see the gospel cost Ephesus fifty thousand drachmas and a trade, so that conversion reads as expensive rather than merely sincere.
He wants us to believe the mission advances through opposition, because the riot ends with a pagan official declaring the Christians guilty of nothing.
